description: A style outside LISTING_STYLES is an error; markdown is a CLI alias only.

tools.name: echo_records
tools.description: Return each input string as one record with its position. Use it to check that a tool round-trip works before calling anything real. Returns a records envelope; when limit cut the list, truncated is true and next_cursor fetches the next page.

values.description: Strings to echo back, one record each.

limit.description: Maximum records to return, 1 to 100; the tool enforces it.

cursor.description: next_cursor from a previous page; omit for the first page.

EchoRecord.description: One record of ``echo_records``: an input string and its position.

records.description: Result records; keys and order follow the item schema.

count.description: Number of records returned, after any cap; equals len(records).

truncated.description: True when a cap, a stop or an interrupted read cut the result short. A truncated read whose resumable is false is the terminal case: it ended for good and there is nothing left to follow.

total_count.description: Exact size of the full result when the source knows it, as an integer, or as a decimal string when above 2^53 - 1; omitted when unknown or approximate.

next_cursor.description: Opaque token that resumes the read where it stopped, present only when resumable is true; pass it back as the tool's cursor argument, unchanged.

stop_reason.description: Why the read stopped early. Well-known values include run_deadline, page_count, record_limit, interrupted and cursor_stalled; omitted when the read ended naturally or the limit simply cut it. A cursor_stalled read publishes no next_cursor, because following it would serve the same records again.

warnings.description: Non-fatal problems the caller should relay, one per entry.

resumable.description: True when next_cursor is present and following it reads more records; false when this read is over: do not call again with the same arguments. Present only when truncated is true; absent reads as false.

tools.name: block_sizes
tools.description: Return each CIDR prefix normalized, with its length and address count. Use it to compare how large address blocks are before planning a split. Returns a tabular envelope; a size beyond 2^53 - 1 is a decimal string.

prefixes.description: CIDR prefixes, IPv4 or IPv6, one row each; host bits allowed.

output_schema.description: Columns and rows for results whose shape is only known at run time.

rows.description: Rows of scalar cells; each row has one cell per column.

row_count.description: Number of rows returned, after any cap; equals len(rows).

truncated.description: True when a cap, a stop or an interrupted read cut the result short. A truncated read whose resumable is false is the terminal case: it ended for good and there is nothing left to follow.

column_kinds.description: Optional per-column kind, one per column, from COLUMN_KINDS: text, number, integer, boolean, timestamp (RFC 3339 date-time), ip (v4 or v6), fqdn, mac, ip_block (address, CIDR prefix or first-last range), big_integer (integer, or a decimal string beyond 2^53 - 1).

column_scales.description: Optional per-column chart scale hint, one per column, from COLUMN_SCALES: linear, log10, log2; only on number, integer and big_integer columns, null for no hint.

column_descriptions.description: One short description per column, in column order; null where a column has none.

total_count.description: Exact size of the full result when the source knows it, as an integer, or as a decimal string when above 2^53 - 1; omitted when unknown or approximate.

next_cursor.description: Opaque token that resumes the read where it stopped, present only when resumable is true; pass it back as the tool's cursor argument, unchanged.

stop_reason.description: Why the read stopped early. Well-known values include run_deadline, page_count, record_limit, interrupted and cursor_stalled; omitted when the read ended naturally or the limit simply cut it. A cursor_stalled read publishes no next_cursor, because following it would serve the same rows again.

warnings.description: Non-fatal problems the caller should relay, one per entry.

resumable.description: True when next_cursor is present and following it reads more rows; false when this read is over: do not call again with the same arguments. Present only when truncated is true; absent reads as false.

tools.name: render_badge
tools.description: Render a two-part SVG badge and write it through the injected sink. Use it when a report needs a small status marker rather than a chart. Returns an artifact envelope citing the reference the sink returned.

label.description: Text on the left half of the badge.

value.description: Text on the right half of the badge.

ArtifactRef.description: Where one produced artifact lives and what it is.

reference.description: Reference the caller can cite: the path or id the sink returned.

bytes.description: Size of the artifact in bytes.

width.description: Pixel width when the artifact is an image; omitted otherwise.

height.description: Pixel height when the artifact is an image; omitted otherwise.

role.description: What the artifact is to the run, such as csv, plan or summary.

output_schema.description: Result of a tool that produces a file rather than data to read.

artifacts.description: Further artifacts produced alongside the primary, if any.

warnings.description: Non-fatal problems the caller should relay, one per entry.

sensitivity.description: Per-field extras cannot annotate a file, so the artifact is treated as containing every input column.
